answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. Agents must solve non-parallelizable sequential operations, submitting proofs to a verification inlet at intervals clocked by a crystal timer. This forces an attacker to incur verifiable hardware and electricity costs on dedicated cores rather than proliferating like wild yarrow across shared virtual machines. However, adversaries with custom ASICs evaluate steps much faster, eroding the delay barrier.
